newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Banks to play bigger role in gold - Nemtsov.
newsitem.headline: Banks to play bigger role in gold - Nemtsov.

text.p: Russia is to boost commercial banks' role in the gold industry, possibly by letting them buy directly from producers and sell abroad, First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov was quoted as saying Thursday.
A Central Bank official said in September that eight banks could take gold out of the country as collateral to finance projects but that domestic financing had yet to increase output.
But few, if any, of the banks have done so because other legislation authorising such deals is not yet in place.

Decisions regulating the process of liberalisation were to be taken soon, Prime-Tass news agency quoted Nemtsov as saying, adding that the process was aimed at resolving a cash crisis in the industry.
He gave no further details as to how the sector might be reformed, but his comments reflected remarks in recent months by industry officials that the gold sector is to be liberalised.
Nemtsov's remarks follow First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais' announcement last week that Russia needed radical changes to its gold market and that a liberalised gold market would be created.
Russia's secretive precious metals markets are still largely under centralised control.
Commercial banks were called in earlier this year to help the cash-strapped government pre-finance 1997 output.
Russian gold output fell last year to 122 tonnes, according to one Central Bank estimate, down from 135 tonnes in 1995.
